chunks: There is the story of the hiding of Musa, the son of Imran from his homeland and his flight from Firon and his people, as mentioned by Quran. No one found him for a long time, neither did they recognize him, until God sent him as an apostle and he made the call to follow him and then the friend and the foe recognized him.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Musa's concealment (ghaybah) before his prophethood?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi utilizes this Quranic precedent to argue that the Imam of the Time’s concealment is not an unprecedented phenomenon, but rather a continuation of the divine pattern seen in Prophet Musa’s hidden years before his public mission. This comparison underscores the theological principle that divine authority often emerges from obscurity, validating the legitimacy of the Mahdi’s ghaybah as a established prophetic model rather than an anomaly.
